name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
summary: Sit tall and press two dumbbells from shoulder height to overhead. Builds the shoulders with less lower-back load than a standing press.
setup: Set the bench upright, or one notch back from vertical. Sit with your back and head against the pad and your feet flat.
Kick the dumbbells up one at a time to shoulder height. Hold them with palms forward or turned slightly in.
Bring your elbows a little in front of your body, about 20 to 30 degrees. This is the scapular plane, the path the shoulder joint moves most freely in.
Stack each wrist straight over its elbow. Elbows sit just below shoulder height.

steps.text: Breathe in and tighten your trunk. Keep your ribs down; do not arch off the pad.
Press the dumbbells up and slightly in, until your arms are straight and the weights are over your shoulders, not in front of your face.
At the top, let your shoulder blades rotate up and your shoulders rise a little toward your ears. Arms end beside your ears.
Lower under control back to shoulder height, forearms vertical, elbows still slightly forward.

jointCues.cue: 20 to 30 degrees in front of your body, under the wrists the whole way.
jointCues.why: Pressing with the elbows pulled straight out to the sides and behind the body pinches the front of the shoulder.

jointCues.cue: Quiet at the start, then let them rotate up and slightly shrug at the top.
jointCues.why: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade makes room for the arm overhead. Forcing them down and back at the top blocks it.

jointCues.cue: Palms forward or turned in a little. If your shoulders feel pinched, turn the palms further in.
jointCues.why: A neutral, palms-in grip lets the upper arm rotate to where the shoulder has the most room.

jointCues.cue: Straight, knuckles to the ceiling, weight over the forearm.
jointCues.why: A bent-back wrist leaks force and strains the joint.

jointCues.cue: Ribs down, back on the pad.
jointCues.why: Arching the lower back turns the movement into an incline press and loads the spine.

breathing: Breathe in at the bottom, breathe out as you press up, breathe in as you lower.
tempo: Press in 1 s, lower in 2 s

mistakes.fault: Elbows flare straight out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Bring them forward until your forearms point straight up from the side and from the front.

mistakes.fault: Lower back arches off the pad
mistakes.fix: Tighten your abs and choose a weight you can press without arching.

mistakes.fault: Dumbbells drift forward in front of the face
mistakes.fix: Finish with the weights over your shoulders and your arms beside your ears.

safety: If you feel a pinch at the front or top of the shoulder, stop above that point and turn your palms in.

cues.text: Wrists stacked over elbows, forearms vertical
Press up and slightly in, ending over the shoulders
At the top, shoulder blades rotate up: a small shrug is right here
